title: Git Hooks and Automation: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on Git hooks: what they are, client-side and server-side hooks, sharing them with core.hooksPath, the pre-commit and husky tools, and how to skip hooks safely.

chapters.title: What Git Hooks Are
points: A hook is an executable script Git runs automatically at a fixed event (commit, push, receive); it is a plain file, any language, with a shebang
Hooks live in .git/hooks/; Git ships *.sample files there and only runs files whose name exactly matches a hook name with no extension
The file must be executable (chmod +x); a non-executable hook is silently ignored
Exit code 0 lets the action continue; non-zero aborts it, but only for hooks that run before the action (pre-*)
Hooks are local and not versioned: .git/hooks is never cloned or pushed, so teammates do not get yours

chapters.title: Client-Side Hooks
points: pre-commit runs before the commit message is requested; non-zero exit aborts the commit; use it for lint, format and fast tests on staged files
prepare-commit-msg runs before the editor opens and can pre-fill the message; commit-msg receives the message file path as $1 and validates it (e.g. Conventional Commits regex)
Example commit-msg: grep -qE '^(feat|fix|chore|docs)(\(.+\))?: .+' "$1" || { echo 'Bad message'; exit 1; }
pre-push runs before pushing to the remote, receives the remote name and URL as arguments, and reads ref info on stdin; use it for the full test suite
post-commit, post-merge and post-checkout run after the action, cannot abort it, and are used for notifications or reinstalling dependencies

chapters.title: Server-Side Hooks
points: Server-side hooks run on the remote repository: pre-receive, update and post-receive
pre-receive runs once per push, reads old-sha new-sha refname lines on stdin; non-zero rejects the entire push
update runs once per branch being pushed and can reject individual refs; its arguments are refname, old-sha, new-sha
post-receive runs after the push is accepted and cannot reject; use it for CI triggers, deploys and notifications
Hosted platforms (GitHub, GitLab) usually do not expose these hooks; use protected branches, required checks or webhooks instead

chapters.title: Sharing Hooks with core.hooksPath
points: git config core.hooksPath .githooks points Git at a tracked folder instead of .git/hooks, so hooks are versioned with the repo
core.hooksPath is local config, so each clone must run the command once, usually via a setup script or make target
Use --global to apply one hooksPath to all repos; this replaces .git/hooks, so a repo's own local hooks stop running
Tracked hook files still need the executable bit; set it with git update-index --chmod=+x .githooks/pre-commit
Check which path is active with git config core.hooksPath; an empty value means the default .git/hooks

chapters.title: Tools: pre-commit and husky
points: pre-commit (Python framework) is configured in .pre-commit-config.yaml listing repo, rev and hook ids; install the git hook once with pre-commit install
pre-commit runs hooks only on staged files by default; pre-commit run --all-files runs them on the whole repo, and pre-commit autoupdate bumps pinned revs
husky (JS ecosystem) stores hooks in .husky/; set it up with npx husky init and add the 'prepare' script so installs enable it automatically
husky works by setting core.hooksPath to .husky/_; put commands such as npx lint-staged in .husky/pre-commit
lint-staged runs linters only on staged files, configured in package.json; a hook that auto-fixes files must re-stage them, which lint-staged does by default
Pick pre-commit for polyglot or Python repos, and husky with lint-staged for Node projects

chapters.title: Skipping Hooks, Mistakes and Cheat Sheet
points: git commit --no-verify (-n) skips pre-commit and commit-msg; git push --no-verify skips pre-push; neither skips server-side hooks
Env var escape hatches: HUSKY=0 disables husky, and SKIP=hook-id skips specific pre-commit hooks while keeping the rest
Mistake: slow pre-commit hooks (full test suite) push people to --no-verify; keep pre-commit fast and move heavy checks to pre-push and CI
Mistake: relying on client-side hooks for enforcement, since they are skippable; always repeat critical checks in CI or server-side
Cheat sheet: pre-commit = lint staged, commit-msg = validate message, pre-push = tests, pre-receive = reject push, core.hooksPath = share, --no-verify = bypass
